content: The seat of the soul is where the inner and the outer worlds meet.
author: Carl Jung
sourceWork: Modern Man in Search of a Soul (1933)
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Carl Jung understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: In what relationship or encounter can you practice seeing beyond outer masks into shared humanity?
